messages:
maria: Heads-up — I sketched a draft for an "autofence + repairflow" that: 1) cordons nodes on high XID/ECC spike, 2) attempts soft-evict (k8s/Slurm-aware), 3) runs a short retry/backoff and health probe, 4) if still bad -> fence + reimage. Wanted feedback on backoff timings and failure-mode signals.

jake: Nice. Can you paste the state machine? short bullets are fine.

sasha: +1 on auto-fence but we should prefer soft-evict for GPU jobs with long checkpoints. Don't want to nuk e everything mid-checkpoint.

yuan: For Slurm we can do `scontrol hold` + drain logic instead of immediate kill. For K8s we have `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`. Keep timeouts conservative for batch.

maria: Agreed. Here's the rough flow I had in mind:
```
STATE: OK -> MONITOR
on XID/ECC rate > threshold -> SOFT_CORDON
SOFT_CORDON: annotate node, trigger workload-aware eviction
  - Try up to 3 soft evict attempts, backoff 30s -> 90s -> 270s
  - Run health probe after each attempt (memtest-lite + nvml query)
if healthy -> UNCORDON
else -> FENCE_AND_REPAIR
FENCE_AND_REPAIR: fence node (powercycle or host-fence), cleanup instance, reimage, return to OK
```

maria: Soft-evict attempt should call platform agent that understands Slurm checkpoint windows and K8s pod disruption budgets.

jake: Those backoff numbers escalate quickly — 30/90/270 = x3. I like exponential but maybe clamp to a max of 5 minutes for interactive clusters. For long-running batch we can allow longer.

dante: We need signal correlation: XID burst + ECC + GPU_temperature spike are stronger together. Single XID alone should trigger only SOFT_CORDON with 1 quick retry.

pri ya: (typo) Priya: ops-bot: can we have a config per "capacity pool"? e.g., preemptible vs reserved: different thresholds and different repair actions.

ops-bot: @pri ya created config proposal: /configs/autofence/pools.yml (pending review) :gear:

maria: Example k8s command sequence we want the agent to run for soft-evict:
```
kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/autofence=soft
kubectl cordon <node>
# allow PDBs, signal workloads to checkpoint via preconfigured hook
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=360 --delete-emptydir-data=false
# if drain fails after backoff attempts -> escalate
```

yuan: For Slurm, mimic with:
```
scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=RESERVED Reason="autofence soft-cordon"
srun --nodes=1 --exclusive --requeue ... # or coordinate with jobmgr to checkpoint
scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=DRAIN
```

sasha: Can we integrate warm fallback routing so user-facing models route off the pool immediately during SOFT_CORDON? Avoid tail latency.

maria: Yes — routing hook included. Also we should rate-limit how many nodes can be in SOFT_CORDON per AZ to avoid capacity cliff. Suggest default max 2 per AZ, override per pool.

jake: Observability: emit events for each state transition, include recent nvml logs, ECC/XID counters, job IDs affected. Make those searchable in Console.

maria: Security/ops question: who can abort a FENCE_AND_REPAIR? Ops + oncall leads only. We need a manual unlock for nodes stuck in FENCE_AND_REPAIR for >30m.

dante: Add a fast-path for nodes in reserved tenant pools: immediate notify but do NOT fence automatically. Some customers will want ops approval.

maria: I pushed a PR with the state machine and a short PoC agent (will link in thread). Main asks: a) agree on backoff numbers (per pool override), b) signals to combine for escalation, c) max parallel soft-cordons per AZ.

pri ya: +1. I'll draft pool defaults (preemptible: aggressive; reserved: lenient).

ops-bot: Incident stub created: AUTOFENCE-1932107777. Please comment PR #548 when ready.

jake: let's sync for 20m after standup to finalize numbers.

maria: cool, I'll update with a matrix and add the nvml probe script snippet. :thumbsup:
